verdict.rationale: Docs imply broad multi-file code work (e.g. the quickstart example asks Slate to review an entire codebase and produce ARCH.md, plus orchestration features for parallelizing tasks across files/agents), suggesting Slate can act on plain-language requests across a codebase. However, independent community scrutiny of a specific real-world claim (a 'ported library' from one sentence) found it was actually a trivial JS->TS rename, excluded tests, lacked a verifiable repo, and drew explicit skepticism about the quality/usefulness of the generated code — concretely contradicting the marketed multi-file code-generation capability. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of a genuine multi-file bug-fix/feature-implementation workflow with verifiable before/after results, and independent hands-on confirmation that resolves the community dispute.
